items.title: Nat Hentoff interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: And you know for example one of the things I was most pleased to do, because the guy died so young, Booker Little. He wrote most of the music, he played trumpet on it, and it was just amazing stuff.

ctx.x: That’s good. When they’d improvise these blues then you’d have to name it something, right?

They’d name it. See one other thing is, the leader of the date was always at the final session, the final cutting session. It was his recording. I wasn’t going to say what tracks we’re going to use etcetera. And you know for example one of the things I was most pleased to do, because the guy died so young, Booker Little.
